THEORY

The titration between bench acid and bench alkali or bench acid and dilute alkali does not give correct titre value. This is because a small volume of the bench acid or bench alkali is consumed by a large volume of the dilute alkali. A very small volumetric error, therefore, gives a different resulting strength. Hence, correct titre value is obtained when the dilute solutions are titrated. For this reason, double titraüon is performed. At first, bench acid is titrated against dilute alkali to have only one rough reading. Then the approximate strength of the bench acid is determined.

The bench acid is diluted to the required extent such that the diluted acid and alkali neutralize more or less in equal volumes. Then second titration is done to standardize this diluted acid solution. By knowing the strength of the diluted acid, the strength of the bench acid can be calculated. The unknown strength is determined using the normality equation, VISI=vgsg Where, Volume of acid (say)
